page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-128 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 virtual CPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The instance is configured with 512 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and public IPv4 addresses are not bundled by default.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and Passmark CPU physics tests. Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores falling into the average to strong categories. Memory bandwidth tests show strong read-only performance for small cached blocks at 6959.33 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds remain average. Cryptographic execution is highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES flags, resulting in a top-tier Passmark CPU encryption score.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is the absence of integrated local storage and dedicated GPUs, which limits its applicability for direct high-speed local disk operations or hardware-accelerated deep learning. However, the high resource density of 128 dedicated vCPUs combined with a standard memory ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy, highly parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory-to-core ratios. This configuration is highly effective for multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, database operations, static web serving, and medium-model LLM prompt processing.
